initialContact.message: I have 18,500€ just sitting in savings account earning basically nothing. I want to start investing but I'm completely lost. Index funds? ETFs? Nordnet? Osakesäästötili? I don't know where to start. I'm 26, good income, no debt - everyone says I should be investing but it seems complicated. Can you explain like I'm 5 how to actually start investing in Finland?

problemContext.currentSituation: Software developer with savings ready to invest but overwhelmed by information and options
problemContext.emotionalState: motivated but confused, information overload, wanting simple start

idealAdvice: Great that you want to start! Let's make this super simple:
- Keep 6 months expenses in savings (~10,000€ for you)
- This stays liquid - don't invest ALL your money
Option A: Osakesäästötili (ASK - Stock Savings Account)
- No taxes until you withdraw money (can compound tax-free)
- Available at: Nordnet, Nordea, OP, others
Recommendation for you: Open ASK at Nordnet (lowest fees, easy to use)
Don't overthink this! Start with ONE index fund:
VWCE (Vanguard FTSE All-World) or similar global index ETF
Either one is fine - don't stress about picking 'perfect' one
This is 'dollar cost averaging' - spreads out risk
7. Don't look at it for 5-10 years
Q: 'Should I wait for market to drop?'
A: No one can time the market. Start now, invest regularly.
Q: 'What if market crashes after I invest?'
A: Keep investing monthly - you buy more shares when cheap!
A: No - you own real companies. Over 20+ years, markets go up.
In 20 years at 7% average: ~56,000€ (without adding more)
That's your retirement fund starting NOW at age 26
Nordnet → ASK → VWCE → 8,500€ + 500€/month → Wait 20 years → Profit
You're a developer - this is like setting up automated deployment and forgetting about it!
commonMistakes: Overcomplicating with multiple funds and strategies
Not explaining ASK tax advantage clearly
Forgetting to mention keeping emergency fund
Making it sound scarier than it is
Missing that he wants 'explain like I'm 5' simplicity
